Kevin / Logan —

Drafting the matrix and methodology below; attaching a CSV (hybrid-load-matrix.csv) and a short appendix (rfi-performance-appendix.pdf). High level summary first, then methodology and test vectors.

Summary (top-level):
- Test environment: Redwood Hosted cluster (region: us-west-2) using m-GPU instance family with our production serving runtime (continuous batching + KV prefix cache).
- Model family used: community LlamaX-34B-8k (quantized path) and a smaller 13B variant for low-latency tiers. We provide both numbers to show delta between variants.
- Workload classes: A=Short-chat (1-3 turns, avg tokens per request 20-80), B=Streaming short responses (token-by-token streaming, 40-250 tokens), C=Long-form (1k, 2k, 4k contexts), D=Embeddings/reranking (dense vector workloads) — matrix covers A/B/C primarily.

Key results (representative):
- Short-chat (A), small tier (13B): p95=38ms, p99=86ms, throughput=350 rps (end-to-end, no streaming) at 95% CPU util target.
- Streaming short (B), small tier (13B): p95 first-token=22ms, steady-state token throughput=1800 tokens/sec per replica, observed p99 tail for token emission under burst=210ms.
- Long-form (C, 2k context), large tier (34B): p95=410ms per token for generation step, end-to-end completion for 2k average generation ~18.5s under target concurrency 40 reqs/sec.
- Graceful degradation: when GPU pool saturated, routing shifts to compatible smaller-quantized variant (34B->13B) with quality-degraded but latency preserved for p95 targets; automatic throttling and 429 backpressure at the API layer for sustained overload.

Methodology (concise):
1) Traffic shaping: we synthesize request streams using a closed-loop load driver that supports arrival processes: Poisson base + scheduled bursts (sine-wave burst, 10s windows, 5x peak).
2) Concurrency sweep: run experiments at concurrency C=[1,5,10,25,50,100,250] per replica across replica counts R=[1,2,4,8] to map throughput frontier.
3) Cold-starts: include separate tests with an idle period of 30+ minutes before spike to capture model cold-start p95/p99; warm runs use steady-state after 5k tokens.
4) Prefix cache: we pre-seed prefix cache with top 5000 most frequent prefixes from a sampled production log to measure cache-hit vs miss behavior; matrix includes both hit and miss columns.
5) Reproducibility: each datapoint is mean of 5 runs, each run 180s of stabilized traffic after warmup; standard deviation and sample counts included in appendix.
6) Instrumentation: token-level traces, server-side per-shard timing, end-to-end tracing via distributed tracing header propagation.

Attachments included: hybrid-load-matrix.csv (rows: workload class, model variant, replica_count, concurrency, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens_per_sec, requests_per_sec, cache_hit_rate), rfi-performance-appendix.pdf (methodology, repeatability notes), sla-latency-defs.xlsx (SLA definition mapping).

Open questions for Acme to finalize numbers:
- Do you prefer streaming-first-token vs end-to-end latency for short-chat in your evaluation? We'll compute both but only one will be highlighted.
- Any regulatory constraints forcing private deployment (if so we'd run on your VPC which changes network variance numbers).

Action items: Logan to deliver CSV + appendix to Kevin by EOD Nov 19. We will include the reproducibility script in the shared Drive.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Perf Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

Quick technical note on graceful-degradation and cache behavior for the matrix (cc Logan):

- Routing policy: we use policy-based routing by latency budget -> when a request's policy indicates low-latency priority, requests route to a smaller variant or to pre-warmed replicas. For mixed-traffic classes, we maintain two queues per replica to prioritize small-chat tokens.
- Cache seeding: the prefix cache seeding approach in Ben's test uses a TTL of 6 hours in the benchmark to simulate warm business hours; for the 60-minute cold-start column we'll purge and cold-seed accordingly.
- Observed artifact: in some burst shapes (5x sine-wave) we saw p99 token emission spike due to backpressure propagation in GPU scheduler; mitigation is to throttle admission and shed least-priority requests (429) while routing priority ones to quantized variants. We will include the measured delta in the matrix and note the mitigation knobs (admission control, routing fallback configs).

I'll add a short note in the appendix on how to interpret the fallback columns and include the routing config we used (policy names and thresholds).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

One-page narrative (copyable):
- We maintain p95 under burst via three levers: (1) smart routing to quantized/compatible variants, (2) prefix caching for frequent conversational paths, and (3) admission control that throttles low-priority requests and preserves latency budgets for high-priority traffic.
- Tests were run across concurrency sweeps and replica counts; each datapoint is the mean of 5 independent runs after warmup.
- Cold-starts measured with a 60-minute idle window; warm-up behavior reported separately to avoid masking steady-state performance.
- Instrumentation traces and scripts are included for reproducibility; we recommend running the driver from a colocated host in your VPC for the most relevant network characteristics.
